mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real GDP (GDPC1) indicates expanding economic activity, boosting corporate earnings expectations and driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of instances when GDPC1 growth is positive, or the correlation between GDPC1 growth and SPX returns is statistically insignificant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decline in unemployment rate below 5.0% signals a tight labor market, reducing wage pressures and increasing corporate profitability, which drives positive S&P 500 returns over 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE is below 5.0%, or the average return in triggered periods is not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: The simultaneous decline in federal funds rate and stable CPI (CPIAUCSL) indicates a monetary easing cycle with low inflation, reducing discount rates and increasing equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 55% of instances when FEDFUNDS declines and CPIAUCSL is stable, or the interaction effect is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: In a monetary tightening cycle (FEDFUNDS rising), the S&P 500 experiences negative returns due to higher discount rates and reduced risk appetite, leading to underperformance over 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when FEDFUNDS rises, or the average return in tightening periods is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A rising employment level (PAYEMS) indicates expanding economic activity and increased consumer spending, driving positive S&P 500 returns over 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 50% of instances when PAYEMS growth is positive, or the correlation between PAYEMS growth and SPX returns is not significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production below 90.0 (relative to 2017=100) signals a contraction in manufacturing output, reducing corporate revenue expectations and causing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when INDPRO is below 90.0, or the average return in triggered periods is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: The joint decline in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicates a weakening consumer demand, leading to reduced corporate earnings forecasts and negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when both HOUST and RSAFS decline, or the interaction effect is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: In a high inflation environment (CPIAUCSL > 3.0% annually), the S&P 500 experiences negative returns due to aggressive central bank policy and reduced real cash flows, leading to underperformance over 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when CPIAUCSL exceeds 3.0%, or the average return in high inflation periods is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).
